newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN CENSUS RESULTS DUE APRIL '97.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN CENSUS RESULTS DUE APRIL '97.

text.p: Detailed results of South Africa's 1996 census will be released in April next year, but prelimianry results should be out by the end of June, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Thursday.

Speaking during the parliamentary debate on the Central Statistical Service's 1997/98 budget, Manuel said the census was now expected to cost the country 398 million rand, up from last year's 356 million rand estimate.
Manuel said the delay in finalising the census had mainly been due to complications in paying census staff, which had delayed the start of processing census forms.

The original target had been December, but Manuel said the fact that the final report would now take 16 months after the census to complete was, by international standards, "quite typical for a country this size."
"In order to meet the interim needs of users, the CSS has for the first time undertaken to produce a preliminary count of men and women, broken down by province, by end-June," he said.
It was also likely that some of the 100,000 short term employees taken on as enumerators had cheated and not tried to visit allocated homes.
